newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-PARMA CUT JUVENTUS'S LEAD TO FOUR POINTS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-PARMA CUT JUVENTUS'S LEAD TO FOUR POINTS.

text.p: Parma injected some life into the Italian title race on Sunday, coming back to beat Atalanta 2-1 to move within four points of leaders Juventus who were held 0-0 at home by Sampdoria.
The win kept alive Parma's hopes of overhauling the Turin club and significantly boosted their chances of finishing second and thus earning a place in next season's Champions' League.
They have 52 points and a four-point cushion over UEFA Cup finalists Internazionale who lost 1-0 at home to Vicenza on Saturday.
Parma, decimated by injuries, had to battle back in Bergamo after Atalanta dominated the first half and took the lead with a controversial goal by Gigi Lentini in the 36th minute.
Parma players erupted in protest after the referee gave the goal, even though the linesman had raised his flag for offside.
The 1995 UEFA Cup winners pulled level when Argentine international striker Hernan Crespo headed home in first half injury time.
Italy's Enrico Chiesa hammered home a fierce angled from five metres in the 66th minute.
In Turin, fourth-placed Sampdoria kept European Cup finalists Juventus on their toes and could have stolen a win had Italy goalkeeper Angelo Peruzzi not made several fine saves.
The Rome derby ended dramatically when Lazio's Igor Protti equalised in the final seconds of injury time after Argentina's Abel Balbo had given Roma the lead after 35 minutes.
